title: Commit a change with Source Control
summary: Stage a changed file, write a message and commit it with Git.

steps.say: Look at the bottom left of the Status Bar. Say done if it shows a branch name such as main.
hints: No branch name means the folder is not a Git repository yet.
In that case the Source Control view offers an Initialize Repository button.
steps.why: Commits need the folder to be a Git repository.

steps.say: Open any file, change one line, and press Control S to save.

checks.prompt: Does the Source Control icon in the Activity Bar show a number badge?

hints: Adding a blank line is enough for practice.
A dot on the tab means the file is not saved yet.
steps.why: Git only sees changes that are saved to disk.

steps.say: Press Control Shift G to open Source Control.

checks.prompt: Is the Source Control view open, listing a changed file under Changes?

hints: Source Control is the branching icon in the Activity Bar, often with a number on it.
Or open the View menu and choose Source Control.
steps.why: This view lists every file that differs from the last commit.

steps.say: Hover over your changed file and click the plus icon called Stage Changes.

checks.prompt: Is the changed file now listed under a Staged Changes heading?

hints: The icon appears only while the mouse is over the file row.
Right-click the file and choose Stage Changes as another route.
steps.why: Staging picks exactly which changes go into the next commit.

steps.say: Click the Message box at the top of the view and type a short description of your change.

checks.prompt: Is there text typed in the message box above the Commit button?

hints: Write what changed, such as Add a blank line to the readme.
Keep it to one line for now.
steps.why: A clear message tells your future self why the change was made.

steps.say: Press Control Enter, or click Commit, to save the snapshot.

checks.prompt: Is the Staged Changes list now empty, with the message box cleared?

hints: If VS Code offers to stage all changes, read the list before agreeing.
The commit stays on this computer until you click Sync Changes or Push.
steps.why: Each commit is a point in history you can return to.
